source: docs/workit-next/host-approval.md (#649, #419): an action that needs the user's yes is approved by the host's prompt on the one plain `workit approve <id>` call, never by a chain, a hand-written grant or another user-only verb

approval_needed: workit git push --release 4.5.0 needs the user's yes. approve: run `workit approve ap_k3m7q2xa` now with your shell tool, as its own call with no cd, pipe or redirect; never ask the user to type it: your call makes the host ask them, and only their answer approves

require.why: the plain call is the only one the host asks on and records

forbid.why: a chain, substitution, env prefix or --cwd around workit approve is denied: the host records nothing
